Machine-readability step (the one for this pass): path index: how each actor reaches the top hubs. Until now a reader who wanted to know "how is X tied to Trump" had to rebuild the graph and search it; the bridge index gave scores, not the routes. powermap.json gains path_index: for every actor with sourced edges (285), the shortest chain of sourced, non-retired edges to each anchor hub (anchors = Donald Trump + the next four by betweenness: Musk, Epstein, Thiel, Binance this run). Fewest hops first; among equally short chains the strongest wins (a small penalty for each I hop, SAID-only hop or sequence-only hop). Each route gives hops, path (names), edge_ids and edge_ns (the #n printed on every map), weakest_grade, counts of I / SAID / sequence hops and all_V; null = not connected. Plus a per-anchor summary (reachable, unreachable, hop histogram, mean hops, all-V chains) and new_nodes_to_trump. Every nodes[] entry gains hops_to_trump and path_to_trump_edge_ids; powermap-nodes.csv gains hops_to_trump and path_to_trump columns; powermap.md gains a "Path index" section; the summary card gets a "PATH INDEX" block (hop histogram to Trump, then each new actor's route with edge numbers) and a zipped PathIndex iTXt chunk (_embed() can drop it from the overview chunk if size demands).
